title: Advising a client: discovery, plain notices, pricing and training

say: Advising a client: discovery, plain-language notices, pricing and staff training.
This is the video for Module 3 of Digital Privacy and Data Protection.
Generic advice fails, because a bakery, a church and a fintech all hold personal data in very different ways. So every engagement starts with discovery.

panel.heading: Find real practice, not stated policy
items: Interview the people who do the work
Ask to see the last form they filled

say: Interview the people who do the work, not only the owner. The receptionist knows where the forms really go.

panel.heading: Find real practice, not stated policy
items: Interview the people who do the work
Ask to see the last form they filled

say: Ask for examples. Show me the last form you filled tells you more than asking if they collect data responsibly.

panel.heading: Find real practice, not stated policy
items: Interview the people who do the work
Ask to see the last form they filled

say: And explain that you are looking for fixes, not culprits. People hide practices they fear will get them blamed.

panel.heading: Find real practice, not stated policy
items: Interview the people who do the work
Ask to see the last form they filled

say: Step one. Send your question set ahead and ask for blank copies of the forms.

Step two. Interview the owner and the staff. For example, Funmi reviewed a school in Lekki. The proprietor said photos were only used with consent, but the admission form just said, I agree to all school policies.
Step three. Walk through reception, offices and the staff room. Funmi found pupils' medical forms, listing allergies, in an open tray.
Take notes, and with permission, photos of settings and locations only. Leave with evidence of the problem, not a copy of it.

panel.heading: Discovery in five moves
panel.rule: Photograph settings and places, never someone's personal data.

say: Step four. Check the forms and tools, such as class WhatsApp groups that show every parent's number to every other parent.

panel.heading: Discovery in five moves
panel.rule: Photograph settings and places, never someone's personal data.

say: Step five. Write a one-page note. For each finding, say what you saw, which principle it affects, and why it matters. End with the three most urgent items.

panel.heading: Discovery in five moves
panel.rule: Photograph settings and places, never someone's personal data.

say: A privacy notice copied from a big company's website describes things that do not happen and misses what does. Write it from your inventory, so it is true and short. Avoid legal phrases like these.

panel.heading: Write it the way you speak
right: We share it with our delivery company
We delete it 12 months after your order
Send MY DATA to our WhatsApp

say: Use we and you, and short sentences. We share your name and address with the delivery company, only to deliver your order. We delete your details 12 months after your last order.
Then test it on three people like the customers. Wherever they hesitate, rewrite.

panel.heading: Write it the way you speak
right: We share it with our delivery company
We delete it 12 months after your order
Send MY DATA to our WhatsApp

say: Clients often say make us compliant, which is not a scope. Offer clear tiers, list what is not included, and price from hours.
Funmi adds up inventory, gap assessment, notice, training and a review meeting. That is 23 hours, at about 10,000 naira, so 230,000 naira.
She adds 15% for unexpected extra work, which is 34,500 naira.
That makes 264,500 naira, which she rounds to 265,000 naira, with 50% on signing and 50% on delivery.
In writing, she excludes legal opinions and NDPC registration filing. You give practical support, not legal opinions.
Policies do not protect data. People do. Start with a short story from their world, like a parent upset that a child's photo was posted.

say: Then teach five house rules.

panel.heading: A 30-minute staff briefing
items: 25 to 30: who to call, one-page summary

say: Practise real scenarios. For a pharmacy: a caller says she is a customer's sister and asks what medicine he collected. The right answer is to share nothing and offer to pass a message.

panel.heading: A 30-minute staff briefing
items: 25 to 30: who to call, one-page summary

say: End by naming who to report incidents to, and hand out a one-page summary.

panel.heading: A 30-minute staff briefing
items: 25 to 30: who to call, one-page summary

say: Lock screens. Share with named people only. Never forward lists to groups. Shred old forms. Report incidents immediately.
And make reporting safe. If staff fear punishment, they hide mistakes, and a hidden breach cannot be reported within 72 hours.

panel.heading: Five habits for every staff member
items: Share files with named people only
Shred forms you no longer need

say: To remember. Check what people say against what really happens. Write notices in plain words. Scope in tiers and list exclusions. Make reporting safe.
And build your portfolio from real or clearly labelled work, with every personal detail removed.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Check stated policy against real practice
Write notices from the inventory, in plain words
Scope in tiers and list exclusions
Build a portfolio with personal data removed

say: Now run a practice discovery interview and write the one-page note. Draft a privacy notice and a one-page proposal. Then prepare your staff briefing and a 90-day plan with one measurable target per phase.
Continue with the lessons below.
